title: 'Move fast, but do it with trust built in': EY CIO tells us why the rapid pace of AI means trust is now a…
excerpt: Delaying digital transformation decisions is no longer possible in the age of AI
content_html:
The rapid growth and evolution of AI technology has led to major shifts in how businesses of all sizes work - but it is also impacting their next big corportate move.

AI has fundamentally changed the risk profile of innovation, as it can expose companies and users to risk earlier, faster and at far greater scale.

Organizations used to be able to afford to delay digital transformation decisions and remain competitive - but now, competitors can use AI to exponentially accelerate while the companies which wait for exact certainty can be left behind before they even begin.

This all means trust is now a crucial business imperative, and organizations must tighten up governance, privacy and security to prevent regulatory and reputational risk - we spoke to Joe Depa, EY Global CIO, to find out more.

  • Many organizations have spent the past two years experimenting with AI, but relatively few have achieved measurable business impact. From EY's perspective, what separates the companies that are delivering tangible ROI from those that remain stuck in what you've described as “pilot purgatory”?

Everyone wants to move faster with AI. The first question is whether they can move fast with trust. The second is how deeply they understand and can optimize the AI value equation.

Trust is what separates the companies getting real ROI from the ones stuck in pilot purgatory. The winners that scale AI successfully across the business tend to share a few characteristics.

They have trusted data as the foundation. Proprietary, secure and well-governed data is becoming one of the biggest competitive moats a company has, because it reflects its unique knowledge, judgment and expertise.

On top of that foundation, they have trusted processes and technology. Data has to be connected to real workflows, real decisions and real business outcomes. The companies pulling ahead don’t use AI to make old processes a little faster. Instead, they rethink how work gets done, where AI can create new value, and how to build governance into the way AI is deployed and scaled.

Then, most importantly, winning organizations invest heavily in helping their workforce expand their skillsets so they can use AI confidently. People won’t use AI if they don’t trust it, and if they don’t use it, they won’t develop the expertise to know where to apply it. That is why upskilling is so important; it’s how you turn employees from passive users into change agents.

Put simply, pilots are great for learning, but being able to progress to scaled adoption is what creates business outcomes. And scaled adoption can only happen when people trust the data, the process, the technology and their own ability to use it well.

That brings us to how to understand and optimize AI value. There’s a lot of focus lately on token costs, but token costs are just one element of the AI value equation. This is a major disconnect that we spotted early in our own business. We saw rising token costs and high-end models being used for low-value work.

In retrospect, it was an important lesson about how measurement priorities change as technologies mature. In the early days of generative AI, the focus was on getting people to use it, so organizations tended to view usage as an indicator of momentum. But now that generative AI models and use cases have become more sophisticated, our focus has shifted to measuring business outcomes.

So we developed a set of best practices to address that. We optimized model selection against the highest value use cases, trained our teams, and put governance around usage. Those strategies enabled us to bring overall token consumption down 60%, while bringing value up. We’ve formalized this in an AI Value Realization Office focused on governance, training and value measurement. The goal is to ensure AI is being applied to the highest-value opportunities and delivering measurable impact.

  • There's often a tension between moving quickly with AI and putting the right controls in place. How can organizations build governance, privacy and security into AI programmes from day one without slowing innovation to the point where they lose competitive advantage?

People often think of governance as the brake, but the opposite is true: having good governance is what gives you the confidence to press the accelerator.

The companies getting it right are building trust into AI from day one, so their teams can move faster without creating risks they have to unwind later.

EY’s Responsible AI Pulse survey found that companies further along in responsible AI are reducing risk and seeing better business outcomes. Nearly four in five reported gains in innovation, and more than half reported revenue growth. Companies with real-time monitoring were also more likely to see improvements in revenue growth and cost savings.

People move faster when they know the guardrails. If employees have a safe, well-governed environment to experiment in, they are much more likely to try new ideas. But if they are worried that every idea could create a compliance issue, they slow down or avoid experimenting altogether.

Governance also matters technically. When controls are added too late, teams often end up with rework, technical debt or pilots that looked promising but cannot scale. Building the right controls early helps avoid that.

Furthermore, once AI agents start to take action, governance can no longer live in a document. It has to be built into the system itself: how access is controlled, how behavior is monitored, how bias is checked and how safeguards kick in when an agent acts.

That is the balance leaders need to strike. Move fast, but do it with trust built in.

  • As AI becomes embedded in core business processes, trust is increasingly seen as a commercial issue rather than simply a compliance one. How are you seeing boards and executive teams rethink governance in light of growing regulatory scrutiny and the potential reputational consequences of AI failures?

Trust is absolutely a commercial issue. If customers, employees or regulators do not trust the products, systems or decisions powered by AI, they will find reasons not to use them. That can affect brand, reputation, operations and growth.

Boards cannot govern what they do not understand. That does not mean every director needs to be a technologist. But boards do need enough AI and technology fluency in the room to ask the right questions, challenge management and understand where the real exposure sits.

We are seeing boards move from asking, “Are we compliant?” to “Where are we exposed?” That is an important shift. Boards are starting to see AI risk more broadly in terms of enterprise risk, in addition to legal and regulatory risk. Agentic AI raises the stakes even more.

For boards, there are three practical next steps.

1. Build AI fluency into the boardroom. Boards need people who understand enough about technology and AI to pressure-test the strategy, the risks and the controls. This doesn’t mean that everyone needs to code, but they do need enough fluency and visibility into leading value indicators to know whether management is asking the right questions.

2. Require visibility across the AI portfolio. Boards should understand where AI is being used, what data it relies on, how material the use case is, who owns it, what resources are being consumed, and what controls are in place. The goal of all this knowledge is to help boards ensure AI is creating business value and that it is being governed at the solution level, the portfolio level and the enterprise level.

3. Make the technical controls real. That means AI-ready data, clear access controls, audit trails, model and agent monitoring, defined escalation paths and the ability to intervene when something behaves outside expectations. Of course, training is absolutely critical to drive adoption of these tools.

  • Many businesses are keen to demonstrate they're embracing AI, but there's a risk of what you've called “innovation theatre.” What are the warning signs that an organisation is investing in AI for appearances rather than driving genuine business transformation, and how can leaders avoid falling into that trap?

The warning sign is when activity gets confused with impact.

A company can have a long list of pilots, demos and proofs-of-concept and still not be creating meaningful value. That is innovation theatre. It looks busy. It may even look impressive. But it does not change the business.

The companies getting this right are much more disciplined. They’ve moved beyond measuring activity to measuring impact on business value. They’re focused on which pilots created value, which scaled successfully, and which improved workflows, customer experiences, risk outcomes or financial performance.

The most successful organizations also establish accountability from the start. Every AI initiative should have a business owner, an investment hypothesis, clear success metrics and AI enabled training that focuses on deploying effectively. Without this, it becomes difficult to separate experimentation from impact.

If pilots are not scaling, leaders need to understand why. Is it a data issue? A trust issue? A weak business case? No clear owner? Not enough transparency or control? Not enough training? Those failure modes tell you where the organization needs to get better.

Disciplined companies avoid the innovation theater trap. Every pilot has an owner, a set of priority metrics and a decision point: scale it, rethink it or kill it.

Otherwise, you end up with a lot of interesting demos and not enough business impact.

  • With AI regulation evolving across different markets and customer expectations around responsible AI continuing to rise, what governance practices do you think will become non-negotiable over the next 12 to 24 months for organisations that want to scale AI responsibly?

AI is moving faster than any one organization, board or regulator can fully keep up with.

That is why leaders don’t have the luxury to wait and see. They need governance models that are resilient enough to adapt across markets, because the regulatory environment will continue to evolve, and it will not evolve the same way everywhere.

Sovereign AI will become a much bigger part of that conversation. Organizations will need to understand where their data lives, how it is protected, who can access it, which models are being used and how those systems align with local laws and market expectations. That goes beyond a technical issue; it’s becoming a board, regulatory and trust issue.

The companies that get this right will focus on a few practical areas.

One is data governance and sovereignty. You need to know what data your AI is using, where it came from, where it is stored and whether it is appropriate for the use case.

Another area of focus is resilience in the operating model. Regulation will keep changing, so governance must be dynamic. Organizations need controls, monitoring, audit trails and escalation paths that can adapt as new rules, risks and expectations emerge. For example, when AI agents are deployed that can make decisions, take action and interact with other systems, regulators will expect organizations to understand how it behaves in the real world.

Lastly, they have an open ecosystem. No company can navigate this complexity alone. Leaders will need to work across regulators, technology providers, advisors, industry groups and academic institutions to separate signal from noise and understand where the market is heading.

Focusing on these areas is how responsible AI evolves from a static set of policies to an enabler. It needs to be designed at the outset into the ways companies manage data, deploy technology, work with regulators and scale innovation across markets. That is how you build trust and resilience at the same time.

  • Looking ahead, do you think trust will become a competitive differentiator in AI adoption? In other words, will organisations that can clearly demonstrate robust governance, transparency and security gain a commercial advantage over those that treat these issues as a compliance exercise?

Yes. Trust is a business necessity, not a checkbox.

The irony is that trust can help companies move faster. When the guardrails and success indicators are clear, teams are freed to innovate with more confidence and less rework.

That is why responsible AI is a growth and innovation driver. If you can show that your AI is governed, explainable, secure and monitored, people are more likely to adopt it, they’ll be far more comfortable scaling it and, most importantly, they’ll be better positioned to scale, differentiate and create value.

That’s the real opportunity: the confidence to move fast in a way everyone, from boards to employees to customers, can trust.

blocks.html_en: Put simply, pilots are great for learning, but being able to progress to scaled adoption is what creates business outcomes. And scaled adoption can only happen when people trust the data, the process, the technology and their own ability to use it well.

sentences.en: Put simply, pilots are great for learning, but being able to progress to scaled adoption is what creates business outcomes.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，试点非常适合学习，但能够逐步扩大采用才能创造业务成果。

sentences.en: And scaled adoption can only happen when people trust the data, the process, the technology and their own ability to use it well.
sentences.zh: 只有当人们信任数据、流程、技术以及他们自己良好使用这些数据的能力时，大规模采用才能实现。

blocks.html_en: That brings us to how to understand and optimize AI value. There’s a lot of focus lately on token costs, but token costs are just one element of the AI value equation. This is a major disconnect that we spotted early in our own business. We saw rising token costs and high-end models being used for low-value work.

sentences.en: That brings us to how to understand and optimize AI value.
sentences.zh: 这给我们带来了如何理解和优化人工智能价值的问题。

sentences.en: There’s a lot of focus lately on token costs, but token costs are just one element of the AI value equation.
sentences.zh: 最近人们非常关注代币成本，但代币成本只是人工智能价值方程式的一个要素。

sentences.en: This is a major disconnect that we spotted early in our own business.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在自己的业务早期发现的一个重大脱节。

sentences.en: We saw rising token costs and high-end models being used for low-value work.
sentences.zh: 我们看到代币成本不断上升，高端模型被用于低价值工作。

blocks.html_en: In retrospect, it was an important lesson about how measurement priorities change as technologies mature. In the early days of generative AI, the focus was on getting people to use it, so organizations tended to view usage as an indicator of momentum. But now that generative AI models and use cases have become more sophisticated, our focus has shifted to measuring business outcomes.

sentences.en: In retrospect, it was an important lesson about how measurement priorities change as technologies mature.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，这是一个关于测量优先级如何随着技术成熟而变化的重要教训。

sentences.en: In the early days of generative AI, the focus was on getting people to use it, so organizations tended to view usage as an indicator of momentum.
sentences.zh: 在生成式人工智能的早期，重点是让人们使用它，因此组织倾向于将使用情况视为动力指标。

sentences.en: But now that generative AI models and use cases have become more sophisticated, our focus has shifted to measuring business outcomes.
sentences.zh: 但现在生成式人工智能模型和用例变得更加复杂，我们的重点已经转向衡量业务成果。

blocks.html_en: So we developed a set of best practices to address that. We optimized model selection against the highest value use cases, trained our teams, and put governance around usage. Those strategies enabled us to bring overall token consumption down 60%, while bringing value up. We’ve formalized this in an AI Value Realization Office focused on governance, training and value measurement. The goal is to ensure AI is being applied to the highest-value opportunities and delivering measurable impact.

sentences.en: So we developed a set of best practices to address that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开发了一套最佳实践来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: We optimized model selection against the highest value use cases, trained our teams, and put governance around usage.
sentences.zh: 我们针对最高价值的用例优化了模型选择，培训了我们的团队，并围绕使用情况进行了治理。

sentences.en: Those strategies enabled us to bring overall token consumption down 60%, while bringing value up.
sentences.zh: 这些策略使我们能够将整体代币消耗量降低 60%，同时提高价值。

sentences.en: We’ve formalized this in an AI Value Realization Office focused on governance, training and value measurement.
sentences.zh: 我们已在人工智能价值实现办公室中将其正式化，专注于治理、培训和价值衡量。

sentences.en: The goal is to ensure AI is being applied to the highest-value opportunities and delivering measurable impact.
sentences.zh: 目标是确保人工智能应用于最高价值的机会并产生可衡量的影响。

blocks.html_en: • There's often a tension between moving quickly with AI and putting the right controls in place. How can organizations build governance, privacy and security into AI programmes from day one without slowing innovation to the point where they lose competitive advantage?

sentences.en: There's often a tension between moving quickly with AI and putting the right controls in place.
sentences.zh: 快速使用人工智能和实施正确的控制之间常常存在紧张关系。

sentences.en: How can organizations build governance, privacy and security into AI programmes from day one without slowing innovation to the point where they lose competitive advantage?
sentences.zh: 组织如何从第一天起就将治理、隐私和安全融入到人工智能项目中，同时又不拖慢创新速度以致失去竞争优势？

blocks.html_en: People often think of governance as the brake, but the opposite is true: having good governance is what gives you the confidence to press the accelerator.

sentences.en: People often think of governance as the brake, but the opposite is true: having good governance is what gives you the confidence to press the accelerator.
sentences.zh: 人们常常认为治理是刹车，但事实恰恰相反：良好的治理才能让你有信心踩下油门。

blocks.html_en: The companies getting it right are building trust into AI from day one, so their teams can move faster without creating risks they have to unwind later.

sentences.en: The companies getting it right are building trust into AI from day one, so their teams can move faster without creating risks they have to unwind later.
sentences.zh: 做对的公司从第一天起就建立了对人工智能的信任，这样他们的团队就可以更快地行动，而不会产生他们必须在以后缓解的风险。

blocks.html_en: EY’s Responsible AI Pulse survey found that companies further along in responsible AI are reducing risk and seeing better business outcomes. Nearly four in five reported gains in innovation, and more than half reported revenue growth. Companies with real-time monitoring were also more likely to see improvements in revenue growth and cost savings.

sentences.en: EY’s Responsible AI Pulse survey found that companies further along in responsible AI are reducing risk and seeing better business outcomes.
sentences.zh: 安永的负责任人工智能脉搏调查发现，在负责任人工智能方面走得更远的公司正在降低风险并看到更好的业务成果。

sentences.en: Nearly four in five reported gains in innovation, and more than half reported revenue growth.
sentences.zh: 近五分之四的受访者表示在创新方面取得了进展，超过一半的受访者表示收入有所增长。

sentences.en: Companies with real-time monitoring were also more likely to see improvements in revenue growth and cost savings.
sentences.zh: 具有实时监控功能的公司也更有可能看到收入增长和成本节约的改善。

blocks.html_en: People move faster when they know the guardrails. If employees have a safe, well-governed environment to experiment in, they are much more likely to try new ideas. But if they are worried that every idea could create a compliance issue, they slow down or avoid experimenting altogether.

sentences.en: People move faster when they know the guardrails.
sentences.zh: 当人们知道护栏时，他们会移动得更快。

sentences.en: If employees have a safe, well-governed environment to experiment in, they are much more likely to try new ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果员工有一个安全、管理良好的环境进行实验，他们就更有可能尝试新想法。

sentences.en: But if they are worried that every idea could create a compliance issue, they slow down or avoid experimenting altogether.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们担心每个想法都会造成合规问题，他们就会放慢速度或完全避免尝试。

blocks.html_en: Governance also matters technically. When controls are added too late, teams often end up with rework, technical debt or pilots that looked promising but cannot scale. Building the right controls early helps avoid that.

sentences.en: Governance also matters technically.
sentences.zh: 治理在技术上也很重要。

sentences.en: When controls are added too late, teams often end up with rework, technical debt or pilots that looked promising but cannot scale.
sentences.zh: 当控制措施添加得太晚时，团队通常会面临返工、技术债务或看似有希望但无法扩展的试点。

sentences.en: Building the right controls early helps avoid that.
sentences.zh: 尽早建立正确的控制措施有助于避免这种情况。

blocks.html_en: Furthermore, once AI agents start to take action, governance can no longer live in a document. It has to be built into the system itself: how access is controlled, how behavior is monitored, how bias is checked and how safeguards kick in when an agent acts.

sentences.en: Furthermore, once AI agents start to take action, governance can no longer live in a document.
sentences.zh: 此外，一旦人工智能代理开始采取行动，治理就不再存在于文档中。

sentences.en: It has to be built into the system itself: how access is controlled, how behavior is monitored, how bias is checked and how safeguards kick in when an agent acts.
sentences.zh: 它必须内置到系统本身中：如何控制访问、如何监控行为、如何检查偏见以及在代理行动时如何启动保护措施。

blocks.html_en: That is the balance leaders need to strike. Move fast, but do it with trust built in.

sentences.en: That is the balance leaders need to strike.
sentences.zh: 这就是领导者需要达到的平衡。

sentences.en: Move fast, but do it with trust built in.
sentences.zh: 行动要快，但要怀有内在的信任。

blocks.html_en: • As AI becomes embedded in core business processes, trust is increasingly seen as a commercial issue rather than simply a compliance one. How are you seeing boards and executive teams rethink governance in light of growing regulatory scrutiny and the potential reputational consequences of AI failures?

sentences.en: As AI becomes embedded in core business processes, trust is increasingly seen as a commercial issue rather than simply a compliance one.
sentences.zh: 随着人工智能嵌入核心业务流程，信任越来越被视为一个商业问题，而不仅仅是一个合规问题。

sentences.en: How are you seeing boards and executive teams rethink governance in light of growing regulatory scrutiny and the potential reputational consequences of AI failures?
sentences.zh: 鉴于日益严格的监管审查和人工智能失败的潜在声誉后果，您如何看待董事会和执行团队重新思考治理？

blocks.html_en: Trust is absolutely a commercial issue. If customers, employees or regulators do not trust the products, systems or decisions powered by AI, they will find reasons not to use them. That can affect brand, reputation, operations and growth.

sentences.en: Trust is absolutely a commercial issue.
sentences.zh: 信任绝对是一个商业问题。

sentences.en: If customers, employees or regulators do not trust the products, systems or decisions powered by AI, they will find reasons not to use them.
sentences.zh: 如果客户、员工或监管机构不信任人工智能驱动的产品、系统或决策，他们就会找到不使用它们的理由。

sentences.en: That can affect brand, reputation, operations and growth.
sentences.zh: 这可能会影响品牌、声誉、运营和增长。

blocks.html_en: Boards cannot govern what they do not understand. That does not mean every director needs to be a technologist. But boards do need enough AI and technology fluency in the room to ask the right questions, challenge management and understand where the real exposure sits.

sentences.en: Boards cannot govern what they do not understand.
sentences.zh: 董事会无法管理他们不理解的事情。

sentences.en: That does not mean every director needs to be a technologist.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着每个主管都需要成为技术专家。

sentences.en: But boards do need enough AI and technology fluency in the room to ask the right questions, challenge management and understand where the real exposure sits.
sentences.zh: 但董事会确实需要足够熟练的人工智能和技术来提出正确的问题、挑战管理层并了解真正的风险所在。

blocks.html_en: We are seeing boards move from asking, “Are we compliant?” to “Where are we exposed?” That is an important shift. Boards are starting to see AI risk more broadly in terms of enterprise risk, in addition to legal and regulatory risk. Agentic AI raises the stakes even more.

sentences.en: We are seeing boards move from asking, “Are we compliant?”
sentences.zh: 我们看到董事会不再询问“我们合规了吗？”

sentences.en: to “Where are we exposed?”
sentences.zh: 到“我们暴露在哪里？”

sentences.en: That is an important shift.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的转变。

sentences.en: Boards are starting to see AI risk more broadly in terms of enterprise risk, in addition to legal and regulatory risk.
sentences.zh: 除了法律和监管风险之外，董事会开始更广泛地将人工智能风险视为企业风险。

sentences.en: Agentic AI raises the stakes even more.
sentences.zh: 代理人工智能进一步提高了风险。

blocks.html_en: For boards, there are three practical next steps.

sentences.en: For boards, there are three practical next steps.
sentences.zh: 对于董事会来说，接下来有三个实际步骤。

blocks.html_en: 1. Build AI fluency into the boardroom. Boards need people who understand enough about technology and AI to pressure-test the strategy, the risks and the controls. This doesn’t mean that everyone needs to code, but they do need enough fluency and visibility into leading value indicators to know whether management is asking the right questions.

sentences.en: Build AI fluency into the boardroom.
sentences.zh: 在董事会中培养人工智能的流畅性。

sentences.en: Boards need people who understand enough about technology and AI to pressure-test the strategy, the risks and the controls.
sentences.zh: 董事会需要对技术和人工智能有足够了解的人来对战略、风险和控制进行压力测试。

sentences.en: This doesn’t mean that everyone needs to code, but they do need enough fluency and visibility into leading value indicators to know whether management is asking the right questions.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着每个人都需要编码，但他们确实需要足够的流畅性和对领先价值指标的可见性，以了解管理层是否提出了正确的问题。

blocks.html_en: 2. Require visibility across the AI portfolio. Boards should understand where AI is being used, what data it relies on, how material the use case is, who owns it, what resources are being consumed, and what controls are in place. The goal of all this knowledge is to help boards ensure AI is creating business value and that it is being governed at the solution level, the portfolio level and the enterprise level.

sentences.en: Require visibility across the AI portfolio.
sentences.zh: 需要整个人工智能产品组合的可见性。

sentences.en: Boards should understand where AI is being used, what data it relies on, how material the use case is, who owns it, what resources are being consumed, and what controls are in place.
sentences.zh: 董事会应该了解人工智能的使用地点、它依赖哪些数据、用例的重要性、谁拥有它、消耗哪些资源以及采取了哪些控制措施。

sentences.en: The goal of all this knowledge is to help boards ensure AI is creating business value and that it is being governed at the solution level, the portfolio level and the enterprise level.
sentences.zh: 所有这些知识的目标是帮助董事会确保人工智能正在创造商业价值，并在解决方案级别、产品组合级别和企业级别对其进行管理。

blocks.html_en: 3. Make the technical controls real. That means AI-ready data, clear access controls, audit trails, model and agent monitoring, defined escalation paths and the ability to intervene when something behaves outside expectations. Of course, training is absolutely critical to drive adoption of these tools.

sentences.en: Make the technical controls real.
sentences.zh: 使技术控制成为现实。

sentences.en: That means AI-ready data, clear access controls, audit trails, model and agent monitoring, defined escalation paths and the ability to intervene when something behaves outside expectations.
sentences.zh: 这意味着人工智能就绪的数据、清晰的访问控制、审计跟踪、模型和代理监控、定义的升级路径以及在某些行为超出预期时进行干预的能力。

sentences.en: Of course, training is absolutely critical to drive adoption of these tools.
sentences.zh: 当然，培训对于推动这些工具的采用绝对至关重要。

blocks.html_en: • Many businesses are keen to demonstrate they're embracing AI, but there's a risk of what you've called “innovation theatre.” What are the warning signs that an organisation is investing in AI for appearances rather than driving genuine business transformation, and how can leaders avoid falling into that trap?

sentences.en: Many businesses are keen to demonstrate they're embracing AI, but there's a risk of what you've called “innovation theatre.”
sentences.zh: 许多企业都热衷于展示他们正在拥抱人工智能，但存在所谓的“创新剧场”的风险。

sentences.en: What are the warning signs that an organisation is investing in AI for appearances rather than driving genuine business transformation, and how can leaders avoid falling into that trap?
sentences.zh: 有哪些警告信号表明组织投资人工智能只是为了外表，而不是推动真正的业务转型？领导者如何避免陷入这个陷阱？

blocks.html_en: The warning sign is when activity gets confused with impact.

sentences.en: The warning sign is when activity gets confused with impact.
sentences.zh: 警告信号是当活动与影响混淆时。

blocks.html_en: A company can have a long list of pilots, demos and proofs-of-concept and still not be creating meaningful value. That is innovation theatre. It looks busy. It may even look impressive. But it does not change the business.

sentences.en: A company can have a long list of pilots, demos and proofs-of-concept and still not be creating meaningful value.
sentences.zh: 一家公司可能拥有一长串试点、演示和概念验证，但仍然无法创造有意义的价值。

sentences.en: That is innovation theatre.
sentences.zh: 那就是创新剧场。

sentences.en: It looks busy.
sentences.zh: 看起来很忙。

sentences.en: It may even look impressive.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能看起来令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: But it does not change the business.
sentences.zh: 但这并不会改变业务。

blocks.html_en: The companies getting this right are much more disciplined. They’ve moved beyond measuring activity to measuring impact on business value. They’re focused on which pilots created value, which scaled successfully, and which improved workflows, customer experiences, risk outcomes or financial performance.

sentences.en: The companies getting this right are much more disciplined.
sentences.zh: 做到这一点的公司更加自律。

sentences.en: They’ve moved beyond measuring activity to measuring impact on business value.
sentences.zh: 他们已经从衡量活动转向衡量对商业价值的影响。

sentences.en: They’re focused on which pilots created value, which scaled successfully, and which improved workflows, customer experiences, risk outcomes or financial performance.
sentences.zh: 他们关注哪些试点创造了价值，哪些试点成功扩展，哪些试点改善了工作流程、客户体验、风险结果或财务绩效。

blocks.html_en: The most successful organizations also establish accountability from the start. Every AI initiative should have a business owner, an investment hypothesis, clear success metrics and AI enabled training that focuses on deploying effectively. Without this, it becomes difficult to separate experimentation from impact.

sentences.en: The most successful organizations also establish accountability from the start.
sentences.zh: 最成功的组织也会从一开始就建立问责制。

sentences.en: Every AI initiative should have a business owner, an investment hypothesis, clear success metrics and AI enabled training that focuses on deploying effectively.
sentences.zh: 每个人工智能计划都应该有一个企业主、一个投资假设、明确的成功指标以及专注于有效部署的人工智能培训。

sentences.en: Without this, it becomes difficult to separate experimentation from impact.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这一点，就很难将实验与影响分开。

blocks.html_en: If pilots are not scaling, leaders need to understand why. Is it a data issue? A trust issue? A weak business case? No clear owner? Not enough transparency or control? Not enough training? Those failure modes tell you where the organization needs to get better.

sentences.en: If pilots are not scaling, leaders need to understand why.
sentences.zh: 如果试点项目没有扩大规模，领导者需要了解原因。

sentences.en: Is it a data issue?
sentences.zh: 是数据问题吗？

sentences.en: A trust issue?
sentences.zh: 信任问题？

sentences.en: A weak business case?
sentences.zh: 业务案例薄弱？

sentences.en: No clear owner?
sentences.zh: 没有明确的主人？

sentences.en: Not enough transparency or control?
sentences.zh: 透明度或控制不够？

sentences.en: Not enough training?
sentences.zh: 训练不够？

sentences.en: Those failure modes tell you where the organization needs to get better.
sentences.zh: 这些失败模式告诉您组织需要在哪些方面改进。

blocks.html_en: Disciplined companies avoid the innovation theater trap. Every pilot has an owner, a set of priority metrics and a decision point: scale it, rethink it or kill it.

sentences.en: Disciplined companies avoid the innovation theater trap.
sentences.zh: 遵守纪律的公司可以避免创新剧场陷阱。

sentences.en: Every pilot has an owner, a set of priority metrics and a decision point: scale it, rethink it or kill it.
sentences.zh: 每个试点都有一个所有者、一组优先级指标和一个决策点：扩展它、重新考虑它或取消它。

blocks.html_en: Otherwise, you end up with a lot of interesting demos and not enough business impact.

sentences.en: Otherwise, you end up with a lot of interesting demos and not enough business impact.
sentences.zh: 否则，您最终会得到很多有趣的演示，但没有足够的业务影响。

blocks.html_en: • With AI regulation evolving across different markets and customer expectations around responsible AI continuing to rise, what governance practices do you think will become non-negotiable over the next 12 to 24 months for organisations that want to scale AI responsibly?

sentences.en: With AI regulation evolving across different markets and customer expectations around responsible AI continuing to rise, what governance practices do you think will become non-negotiable over the next 12 to 24 months for organisations that want to scale AI responsibly?
sentences.zh: 随着人工智能监管在不同市场的发展以及客户对负责任人工智能的期望持续上升，您认为对于想要负责任地扩展人工智能的组织来说，哪些治理实践在未来 12 到 24 个月内将变得不可协商？

blocks.html_en: AI is moving faster than any one organization, board or regulator can fully keep up with.

sentences.en: AI is moving faster than any one organization, board or regulator can fully keep up with.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的发展速度比任何一个组织、董事会或监管机构都无法完全跟上。

blocks.html_en: That is why leaders don’t have the luxury to wait and see. They need governance models that are resilient enough to adapt across markets, because the regulatory environment will continue to evolve, and it will not evolve the same way everywhere.

sentences.en: That is why leaders don’t have the luxury to wait and see.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么领导者没有闲暇观望的原因。

sentences.en: They need governance models that are resilient enough to adapt across markets, because the regulatory environment will continue to evolve, and it will not evolve the same way everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们需要具有足够弹性以适应不同市场的治理模式，因为监管环境将继续发展，而且不会在任何地方都以同样的方式发展。

blocks.html_en: Sovereign AI will become a much bigger part of that conversation. Organizations will need to understand where their data lives, how it is protected, who can access it, which models are being used and how those systems align with local laws and market expectations. That goes beyond a technical issue; it’s becoming a board, regulatory and trust issue.

sentences.en: Sovereign AI will become a much bigger part of that conversation.
sentences.zh: 主权人工智能将成为这场对话的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Organizations will need to understand where their data lives, how it is protected, who can access it, which models are being used and how those systems align with local laws and market expectations.
sentences.zh: 组织需要了解他们的数据存放在哪里、如何保护数据、谁可以访问数据、正在使用哪些模型以及这些系统如何符合当地法律和市场预期。

sentences.en: That goes beyond a technical issue; it’s becoming a board, regulatory and trust issue.
sentences.zh: 这超出了技术问题的范围。它正在成为一个董事会、监管和信任问题。

blocks.html_en: The companies that get this right will focus on a few practical areas.

sentences.en: The companies that get this right will focus on a few practical areas.
sentences.zh: 做到这一点的公司将专注于一些实际领域。

blocks.html_en: One is data governance and sovereignty. You need to know what data your AI is using, where it came from, where it is stored and whether it is appropriate for the use case.

sentences.en: One is data governance and sovereignty.

content_html_zh:
人工智能技术的快速增长和发展已经导致各种规模的企业运作方式发生重大转变，但它也影响着他们的下一个重大企业举措。

人工智能从根本上改变了创新的风险状况，因为它可以让公司和用户更早、更快、更大规模地面临风险。

过去，组织能够推迟数字化转型决策并保持竞争力，但现在，竞争对手可以利用人工智能呈指数级加速，而等待确切确定性的公司可能在开始之前就被抛在后面。

这一切都意味着信任现在已成为至关重要的业务需求，组织必须加强治理、隐私和安全，以防止监管和声誉风险 - 我们采访了安永全球首席信息官 Joe Depa，以了解更多信息。

  • 过去两年，许多组织都在尝试人工智能，但取得可衡量的业务影响的组织相对较少。 从安永的角度来看，那些正在提供切实投资回报的公司与那些仍然深陷你所描述的“试点炼狱”的公司有何区别？

每个人都希望通过人工智能更快地发展。 第一个问题是他们能否带着信任快速行动。 第二是他们对人工智能价值方程的理解和优化能力有多深。

信任是获得真正投资回报率的公司与陷入试点炼狱的公司的区别所在。 在整个企业中成功扩展人工智能的赢家往往具有一些共同特征。

他们以可信数据为基础。 专有、安全且管理良好的数据正在成为公司最大的竞争护城河之一，因为它反映了公司独特的知识、判断和专业知识。

在此基础上，他们拥有值得信赖的流程和技术。 数据必须与真实的工作流程、真实的决策和真实的业务成果相关联。 领先的公司并没有使用人工智能来让旧流程更快一些。 相反，他们重新思考如何完成工作、人工智能可以在哪里创造新价值，以及如何将治理纳入人工智能的部署和扩展方式。

然后，最重要的是，获胜的组织投入巨资帮助员工扩展技能，以便他们能够自信地使用人工智能。 如果人们不信任人工智能，他们就不会使用它；如果他们不使用它，他们就不会发展专业知识来知道在哪里应用它。 这就是为什么提升技能如此重要；这就是将员工从被动用户转变为变革推动者的方法。

简而言之，试点非常适合学习，但能够逐步扩大采用才能创造业务成果。 只有当人们信任数据、流程、技术以及他们自己良好使用这些数据的能力时，大规模采用才能实现。

这给我们带来了如何理解和优化人工智能价值的问题。 最近人们非常关注代币成本，但代币成本只是人工智能价值方程式的一个要素。 这是我们在自己的业务早期发现的一个重大脱节。 我们看到代币成本不断上升，高端模型被用于低价值工作。

回想起来，这是一个关于测量优先级如何随着技术成熟而变化的重要教训。 在生成式人工智能的早期，重点是让人们使用它，因此组织倾向于将使用情况视为动力指标。 但现在生成式人工智能模型和用例变得更加复杂，我们的重点已经转向衡量业务成果。

因此，我们开发了一套最佳实践来解决这个问题。 我们针对最高价值的用例优化了模型选择，培训了我们的团队，并围绕使用情况进行了治理。 这些策略使我们能够将整体代币消耗量降低 60%，同时提高价值。 我们已在人工智能价值实现办公室中将其正式化，专注于治理、培训和价值衡量。 目标是确保人工智能应用于最高价值的机会并产生可衡量的影响。

  • 快速使用人工智能和实施正确的控制之间常常存在紧张关系。 组织如何从第一天起就将治理、隐私和安全融入到人工智能项目中，同时又不拖慢创新速度以致失去竞争优势？

人们常常认为治理是刹车，但事实恰恰相反：良好的治理才能让你有信心踩下油门。

做对的公司从第一天起就建立了对人工智能的信任，这样他们的团队就可以更快地行动，而不会产生他们必须在以后缓解的风险。

安永的负责任人工智能脉搏调查发现，在负责任人工智能方面走得更远的公司正在降低风险并看到更好的业务成果。 近五分之四的受访者表示在创新方面取得了进展，超过一半的受访者表示收入有所增长。 具有实时监控功能的公司也更有可能看到收入增长和成本节约的改善。

当人们知道护栏时，他们会移动得更快。 如果员工有一个安全、管理良好的环境进行实验，他们就更有可能尝试新想法。 但如果他们担心每个想法都会造成合规问题，他们就会放慢速度或完全避免尝试。

治理在技术上也很重要。 当控制措施添加得太晚时，团队通常会面临返工、技术债务或看似有希望但无法扩展的试点。 尽早建立正确的控制措施有助于避免这种情况。

此外，一旦人工智能代理开始采取行动，治理就不再存在于文档中。 它必须内置到系统本身中：如何控制访问、如何监控行为、如何检查偏见以及在代理行动时如何启动保护措施。

这就是领导者需要达到的平衡。 行动要快，但要怀有内在的信任。

  • 随着人工智能嵌入核心业务流程，信任越来越被视为一个商业问题，而不仅仅是一个合规问题。 鉴于日益严格的监管审查和人工智能失败的潜在声誉后果，您如何看待董事会和执行团队重新思考治理？

信任绝对是一个商业问题。 如果客户、员工或监管机构不信任人工智能驱动的产品、系统或决策，他们就会找到不使用它们的理由。 这可能会影响品牌、声誉、运营和增长。

董事会无法管理他们不理解的事情。 这并不意味着每个主管都需要成为技术专家。 但董事会确实需要足够熟练的人工智能和技术来提出正确的问题、挑战管理层并了解真正的风险所在。

我们看到董事会不再询问“我们合规了吗？” 到“我们暴露在哪里？” 这是一个重要的转变。 除了法律和监管风险之外，董事会开始更广泛地将人工智能风险视为企业风险。 代理人工智能进一步提高了风险。

对于董事会来说，接下来有三个实际步骤。

1. 在董事会中培养人工智能的流畅性。 董事会需要对技术和人工智能有足够了解的人来对战略、风险和控制进行压力测试。 这并不意味着每个人都需要编码，但他们确实需要足够的流畅性和对领先价值指标的可见性，以了解管理层是否提出了正确的问题。

2. 需要整个人工智能产品组合的可见性。 董事会应该了解人工智能的使用地点、它依赖哪些数据、用例的重要性、谁拥有它、消耗哪些资源以及采取了哪些控制措施。 所有这些知识的目标是帮助董事会确保人工智能正在创造商业价值，并在解决方案级别、产品组合级别和企业级别对其进行管理。

3. 使技术控制成为现实。 这意味着人工智能就绪的数据、清晰的访问控制、审计跟踪、模型和代理监控、定义的升级路径以及在某些行为超出预期时进行干预的能力。 当然，培训对于推动这些工具的采用绝对至关重要。

  • 许多企业都热衷于展示他们正在拥抱人工智能，但存在所谓的“创新剧场”的风险。 有哪些警告信号表明组织投资人工智能只是为了外表，而不是推动真正的业务转型？领导者如何避免陷入这个陷阱？

警告信号是当活动与影响混淆时。

一家公司可能拥有一长串试点、演示和概念验证，但仍然无法创造有意义的价值。 那就是创新剧场。 看起来很忙。 它甚至可能看起来令人印象深刻。 但这并不会改变业务。

做到这一点的公司更加自律。 他们已经从衡量活动转向衡量对商业价值的影响。 他们关注哪些试点创造了价值，哪些试点成功扩展，哪些试点改善了工作流程、客户体验、风险结果或财务绩效。

最成功的组织也会从一开始就建立问责制。 每个人工智能计划都应该有一个企业主、一个投资假设、明确的成功指标以及专注于有效部署的人工智能培训。 如果没有这一点，就很难将实验与影响分开。

如果试点项目没有扩大规模，领导者需要了解原因。 是数据问题吗？ 信任问题？ 业务案例薄弱？ 没有明确的主人？ 透明度或控制不够？ 训练不够？ 这些失败模式告诉您组织需要在哪些方面改进。

遵守纪律的公司可以避免创新剧场陷阱。 每个试点都有一个所有者、一组优先级指标和一个决策点：扩展它、重新考虑它或取消它。

否则，您最终会得到很多有趣的演示，但没有足够的业务影响。

  • 随着人工智能监管在不同市场的发展以及客户对负责任人工智能的期望持续上升，您认为对于想要负责任地扩展人工智能的组织来说，哪些治理实践在未来 12 到 24 个月内将变得不可协商？

人工智能的发展速度比任何一个组织、董事会或监管机构都无法完全跟上。

这就是为什么领导者没有闲暇观望的原因。 他们需要具有足够弹性以适应不同市场的治理模式，因为监管环境将继续发展，而且不会在任何地方都以同样的方式发展。

主权人工智能将成为这场对话的重要组成部分。 组织需要了解他们的数据存放在哪里、如何保护数据、谁可以访问数据、正在使用哪些模型以及这些系统如何符合当地法律和市场预期。 这超出了技术问题的范围。它正在成为一个董事会、监管和信任问题。

做到这一点的公司将专注于一些实际领域。

一是数据治理和主权。 您需要知道您的人工智能正在使用哪些数据、数据来自何处、存储在何处以及是否适合用例。

另一个关注领域是运营模式的弹性。 监管会不断变化，因此治理必须是动态的。 组织需要能够适应新规则、风险和期望出现的控制、监控、审计跟踪和升级路径。 例如，当部署可以做出决策、采取行动并与其他系统交互的人工智能代理时，监管机构将期望组织了解其在现实世界中的行为方式。

最后，他们拥有开放的生态系统。 没有一家公司能够独自应对这种复杂性。 领导者需要与监管机构、技术提供商、顾问、行业团体和学术机构合作，将信号与噪音分开，并了解市场的发展方向。

关注这些领域是负责任的人工智能如何从一组静态政策演变为推动者的过程。 它需要从一开始就被设计成公司管理数据、部署技术、与监管机构合作以及跨市场规模创新的方式。 这就是您同时建立信任和韧性的方法。

  • 展望未来，您认为信任会成为人工智能采用的竞争优势吗？ 换句话说，与那些将这些问题视为合规行为的组织相比，能够清楚地展示稳健治理、透明度和安全性的组织是否会获得商业优势？

是的。 信任是商业必需品，而不是复选框。

具有讽刺意味的是，信任可以帮助公司更快地发展。 当护栏和成功指标明确时，团队就可以更加自信地进行创新，减少返工。

这就是为什么负责任的人工智能是增长和创新的驱动力。 如果你能证明你的人工智能是受治理的、可解释的、安全的和受监控的，人们就更有可能采用它，他们会更轻松地扩展它，最重要的是，他们将能够更好地扩展、差异化和创造价值。

这才是真正的机会：有信心以每个人（从董事会、员工到客户）都可以信任的方式快速行动。
